caption_or_description: An object held close to a wall casts a sharp shadow because light coming from slightly different directions does not spread out much behind the object. As the object is moved farther away from the wall, the penumbra grows and the umbra becomes smaller. When the object is even farther away, the shadow is less distinct. When the object is very far away (not shown), no shadow is evident because the penumbra expands into a big blur.

caption_or_description: (Interactive Figure) (a) A full Moon is seen when Earth is between the Sun and the Moon. (b) When this alignment is perfect, the Moon is in Earth's shadow, and a lunar eclipse is produced. (c) A new Moon occurs when the Moon is between the Sun and Earth. (d) When this alignment is perfect, the Moon's shadow falls on part of Earth to produce a solar eclipse.

caption_or_description: (Interactive Figure) Details of a solar eclipse. A total eclipse is seen by observers in the umbra, and a partial eclipse is seen by observers in the penumbra. Most Earth observers see no eclipse at all.
